text: No matter how you choose to delineate your evolutionary system of interest. <break time="0.8s" /> , lets say it is cell phones. <break time="0.8s" /> There will be some things. <break time="0.8s" /> That your model just needs to take as a given. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as the fact that new ideas emerge at particular times. <break time="0.8s" /> Indeed. <break time="0.8s" /> All models must make simplifying assumptions of this nature. <break time="0.8s" /> When Wallace and Darwin presented their verbal model of biological evolution. <break time="0.8s" /> There was little knowledge of how variation generation and inheritance worked. <break time="0.8s" /> They just took as a given. <break time="0.8s" /> That these things happened somehow. <break time="0.8s" /> Even at the finest level of detail. <break time="0.8s" /> We need simplifying assumptions. <break time="0.8s" /> Physicists, for example. <break time="0.8s" /> Must take as a given. <break time="0.8s" /> The mass and charge of fundamental particles. <break time="0.8s" /> In a model of atomic bonds. <break time="0.8s" /> Physicists do not attempt to explain. <break time="0.8s" /> Why electrons have their particular mass and charge. <break time="0.8s" /> They just accept the measured values. <break time="0.8s" /> And move on. <break time="0.8s" /> The key point is that we can build useful models. <break time="0.8s" /> At one level of analysis. <break time="0.8s" /> Without a complete accounting of what is happening at all other levels.
